chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I went to him, greeted him, and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! What do you say about a man who dies and has no heir except a brother from breastfeeding, who would inherit him?' He said, 'Yes. My father informed me from his grandfather that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever drinks from our milk or breastfeeds a child for us, then we are his fathers.'
ai.seo_question: Does breastfeeding create an inheritance right equivalent to biological fatherhood in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) confirms that breastfeeding establishes a permanent kinship bond (radāʿ) equivalent to biological parenthood, granting the breastfeeder inheritance rights as a father. It traces this ruling back to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) via his father Imam al-Hasan and grandfather Imam al-Husayn, emphasizing the continuity of legal authority in Shia tradition. The ruling underscores the social and legal weight of wet-nursing in early Islamic society, where milk kinship created prohibitions on marriage and inheritance obligations similar to blood relations.
